Prevention: Prevention is particulaly important as the weed is difficult to control.
Seeds and plant parts with nodes are the main means of spread
Clean tools and farm machinery after leaving an infested area to prevent seeds and plant parts being spread
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. soil on planting stock from contaminated areas; especially important if you do not have the weed on your farm yet.
Monitoring: Inspect fields weekly to assess the levels of infestation, especially during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when found
Direct Control: Place organic mulch (such as rice straw) over the areas where weed is expect to grow, this provides temporary suppression of growth
Inter row cultivation with bullock pulled harrow can provide good control, especially during dry weather
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
